chunks: And ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah narrated from him, peace be upon him:
That he asked him about a man who gets a nosebleed while he is in salat (prayer), and he has already performed part of his salat (prayer).

So he said: "If the water is on his right, or on his left, or behind him, then let him wash it without turning, and let him continue his salat (prayer). But if he does not find the water without turning, then let him repeat the salat (prayer)."
He said: "And vomiting is like that.

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water used to wash away the impurity
key_terms.يَلْتَفِتَ: to turn away or turn around during prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone gets a nosebleed or vomits during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who experiences a nosebleed during salat (prayer) after having completed part of it. If he can wash the blood without turning away, he continues the prayer; otherwise, he repeats it. The same ruling applies to vomiting.
